In [[cryptography]], '''SC2000''' is a [[block cipher]] invented by a research group at [[Fujitsu]] Labs. It was submitted to the [[NESSIE]] project, but was not selected. It was among the cryptographic techniques recommended for Japanese government use by [[CRYPTREC]] in 2003; however, it was dropped to "candidate" by CRYPTREC revision in 2013.

The algorithm uses a key size of 128, 192, or 256 bits. It operates on blocks of 128 bits using 6.5 or 7.5 rounds of encryption. Each round consists of [[substitution box|S-box]] lookups, key additions, and an unkeyed two-round [[Feistel cipher|Feistel network]]. There are 3 S-boxes: a 4×4-bit one used at the beginning of each round, a 5×5-bit one and a 6×6-bit one used in the Feistel network.

No [[cryptanalysis|analysis]] of the full SC2000 has been announced, but a reduced version of 4.5 rounds is susceptible to [[linear cryptanalysis]], and a reduced version of 5 rounds is susceptible to [[differential cryptanalysis]].<ref>{{cite journal
    | author = [[Lars Ramkilde Knudsen|Lars Knudsen]], Håvard Raddum
    | title = A first report on Whirlpool, NUSH, SC2000, Noekeon, Two-Track-MAC and RC6
    | date = 7 March 2001
    | url = https://www.cosic.esat.kuleuven.be/nessie/reports/phase1/uibwp3-007b.pdf
    | access-date = 8 February 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite conference
    | author = Hitoshi Yanami, Takeshi Shimoyama, [[Orr Dunkelman]]
    | title = Differential and Linear Cryptanalysis of a Reduced-Round SC2000
    | conference = Proceedings of Second Open NESSIE Workshop
    | date = 2000
    | url = http://citeseer.ist.psu.edu/yanami00differential.html
    | format = PDF/[[PostScript]]
    | access-date = 8 February 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
    | author = Jiqiang Lu
    | title = Differential Attack on Five Rounds of the SC2000 Block Cipher.
    | journal = Journal of Computer Science and Technology 
    | date = July 2011
    | url = https://sites.google.com/site/jiqiang/JCST26.pdf
    | access-date = 30 January 2012 }}</ref>

In 2014, [[Alex Biryukov]] and Ivica Nikolić found a weakness in the [[key schedule]] of SC2000 which allows an attacker to find colliding keys which result in identical encryptions in just 2<sup>39</sup> time for 256 bit keys. They proved that there are 2<sup>68</sup> colliding key pairs and the whole set can be found in 2<sup>58</sup> time.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Alex Biryukov |author2=Ivica Nikolić |date=10 November 2014 |title=Colliding Keys for SC2000-256 |url=http://orbilu.uni.lu/bitstream/10993/18750/1/biryukov-nikolic-colliding%20keys-sc2000-sac2014.pdf |archive-date=24 September 2016 |access-date=16 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924100248/http://orbilu.uni.lu/bitstream/10993/18750/1/biryukov-nikolic-colliding%20keys-sc2000-sac2014.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>
